extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, judges, and advanced law students concerned with remedies and accounting in patent infringement suits
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing awards of profits, interest, and damages in patent-infringement suits, and the conduct of accountings (masters, evidence, scope, apportionment, and related procedural issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of defendant's profits (scope and period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plaintiff is entitled to recover all profits derived by the defendant through his infringing acts, from the date of the issue or re-issue of the patent to the date of the accounting, irrespective of the price paid by the plaintiff for the patent or the royalties due from him to his licensor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period runs to the time of taking the account; the account may be extended down to the time of the hearing before the master. When the patent was antedated under the Act of 1836, the defendant was liable for all profits after the time to which it was antedated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest on profits — equity vs law distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the plaintiff can recover interest on profits depends on how the profits have accrued: in equity profits are regarded as a debt and bear interest from the time they appear as money or money value in the hands of the defendant; in actions at law profits treated as unliquidated until ascertained by verdict and thus typically do not carry interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the defendant receives price for products sold, the profit portion is property of plaintiff and interest should be allowed while it remains in defendant's possession. If profit results from savings not recognized as money until annual balance, interest computation may begin at that balance date. Decisions are not uniform; distinctions must be kept in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest on royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest on royalties is allowed from the date of the infringement to the date of the decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest on a license/royalty-based measure of damages may be allowed from interlocutory decree date; cases illustrate different starting points (master's report, account termination, interlocutory decree).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest not generally allowed on unliquidated damages until decree
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest is not to be computed on profits or damages until after the decree, especially when the defendant has acted in good faith under his own patent; profits are not regarded as unliquidated damages in some contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where profits are treated as unliquidated damages in law, interest may not be allowed before verdict; in equity, profits often bear interest from detection/receipt. Specific authorities vary; check circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of counsel fees from profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel fees and other litigation expenses are not included in the estimate of profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profits represent gains from the invention; litigation costs are separate and not recoverable as part of profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profits are not trebled (but damages may be)
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits cannot be trebled by the court as damages may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although courts may treble damages in appropriate cases, the statutory/accounting measure for profits does not permit trebling of the profits award itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable damages in addition to profits (Act of 1870)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of July 8, 1870 authorized equity courts to award damages in addition to profits, to afford the plaintiff adequate compensation where profits are no measure of full injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity may grant damages when defendant made no profits or profits insufficient; damages must be proved by evidence and the act does not restrict the court from awarding gains, savings, or advantages recoverable before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trebling and enhancement of damages in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may treble damages in equity as well as at law, and where infringement is flagrant the damages will be trebled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts exercise discretion; if defendant believed himself right or litigated vigorously, courts often decline to enhance damages on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: When damages in addition to profits are allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If profits do not fully compensate the plaintiff because defendant made no profit or less than fair profit, or because injuries lie outside mere loss of profits, additional damages may be awarded to give complete compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages must be established by evidence, not conjecture. Nominal damages may be awarded if neither profits nor damages can be proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of value of infringement (date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of an infringement is its value at the date of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule guides assessment of profits or damages tied to the infringement date rather than later valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior official holdings on liability for profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Supreme Court had held a patent invalid and afterwards sustained it, the infringer is liable for profits arising from his use of the invention after the first decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical case law (e.g., Tilghman v. Proctor) informs when profit liability accrues amid changing validity determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting limited by bill's time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When the bill limits the time of the infringement, the account cannot go beyond it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of the accounting follows the pleadings and decretal order; ambiguity may require court instructions to the master.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment among several defendants and partial liability
rubrics_metrics.description: If not all defendants infringed during the whole time, profits are to be apportioned accordingly; a defendant's liability is limited to the amount accruing while he engaged in the infringing acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When partners or multiple parties are involved, awards may be joint up to the time of a change in membership; apportionment follows periods of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate and successor liability limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits received by one corporation are not collectible from its successor regardless of identity of enterprise or membership; a defendant corporation is not liable for profits made by a preceding corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate succession does not automatically transfer profit liability; examine corporate continuity and applicable authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of officers and government actors
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer who voluntarily uses an invention of no value except for governmental purposes must account for its advantages even if he paid the entire sum to his superior; where the United States is defendant and made no profits except by saving expense, its officers may be accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials cannot escape accounting for voluntary infringements by merely paying receipts to superiors; specifics depend on facts and cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estate liability and death of infringer
rubrics_metrics.description: The death of an infringer does not bar the owner's right to an account from his estate, and a bill of revivor will continue proceedings against the personal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings continue against estate; courts have allowed revival and continued accounting actions post-death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee's right to full profits despite royalty arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee can recover the entire profits whatever royalty arrangements he may have with the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments made by others for past infringements do not guide the profits to be awarded now; awards are based on actual profits attributable to infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that use of invention was beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the defendant has practised the invention raises a presumption that its use was beneficial; this presumption is not overcome by a bare assertion in his answer that the infringement was unprofitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because defendant unlawfully appropriated plaintiff's property, he must disclose enterprise details; plaintiff may obtain an account even if the accounting might show no gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff's burden of proof on the accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The plaintiff must furnish sufficient testimony to enable the master to arrive at definite conclusions and cannot rely upon the master to suggest what proof may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defendant's books show mixed sales (some infringing, some not), the plaintiff must by other testimony separate those which infringed; proof, not conjecture, is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's scope: accept prior findings, not relitigate infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking the account the master has no right to consider the question of infringement or the scope and meaning of the patent, but must accept these matters as they have been already settled by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The master may inspect articles sold or used to determine what proportion of gains is attributable to the patented features, but otherwise should not explore the history or origin of the devices beyond the court's findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's evidentiary powers and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The master must receive all relevant and material evidence, collate and compare it, ascertain data for computation, and formulate a specific monetary award for profits or damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He may examine defendants, inspect books, and compel production by subpoena; if the defendant fails to appear for accounting, the master proceeds ex parte unless the defendant's evidence or books are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for notice, production, adjournment, and contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: The master gives notice of the accounting day to parties or counsel; the master may order the defendant to furnish an account by a certain day and adjourn the hearing; personal service of orders and orders to produce may be followed by attachment for contempt if defendant fails to appear or produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be made by any disinterested person and need not be by the marshals; courts expect reasonable steps to procure presence and production before contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's report, exceptions, and court review
rubrics_metrics.description: The master prepares a draft report from testimony, parties file objections, the master may reconsider and file a final report; either party may file exceptions and have the entire evidence laid before the court which may review facts and law and recommit, set aside, alter, or reverse the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the proceeding the master must be guided by the terms of the decree ordering the account; if ambiguous he may call upon the court for more definite instructions or report back for specific directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master may act beyond territorial jurisdiction to take evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The master may act beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the court, and even in foreign countries, to take evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have approved masters taking evidence in other territories where appropriate; master should choose the best and cheapest method of taking evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits where profits cannot be fixed by evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When the profits cannot be fixed by evidence they cannot be recovered as damages; when neither damages nor profits can be proved, nominal damages may be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confusion of accounts is not confusion of goods; items that infringe must be separated by evidence. On a bill pro confesso, if no satisfactory proof of damages and profits is given on reference, plaintiff may recover only nominal damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master must apply state of the art and other inquiries relevant to profits
rubrics_metrics.description: In pursuing inquiries into damages or profits the master may be led into investigations as to the state of the art at the time of the invention and other kindred subjects to determine attribution of gains to the patented features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State of the art at invention date is material to profit questions; the master may inspect defendant's articles to ascertain whether the infringing features produced the gains.
